name: Positive and negative sides of each functional state
oneLine: Every functional ego state - even Nurturing Parent - has a healthy (positive/OK) and an unhealthy (negative/not-OK) version; none of the five is automatically the "good" one.
whatYouDid: You had to tell Priti's warm, smiling takeover of Sam's work apart from Rhea's flat, firm "you're off rotation" - and recognize that the smile was the smother, and the firmness was the care.
confusion: People assume Nurturing Parent is always the nice one and Controlling Parent is always the harsh one; the tell is that negative Nurturing Parent discounts the other person just as much as negative Controlling Parent does - it just does it by taking over or deciding for them instead of by criticizing them.

fromBook.quote: Positive Nurturing Parent implies caring which is provided from a position of genuine regard for the person helped.

expand.definition: Positive/OK Adapted Child, Free Child, Controlling Parent and Nurturing Parent are all productive uses of that functional part; negative/not-OK versions of the same parts discount, squash, smother or endanger - valence is a second axis, independent of which of the five parts is in use.
expand.otherFraming: The classic example of negative Nurturing Parent is the "smother-mother" who takes the work out of someone's hands instead of asking if they want help - helping from one-up, not alongside.
expand.tryThisToday: Before you help someone today, ask out loud whether they want it - that single question is often the line between positive and negative Nurturing Parent.
